newsitem.title: USA: Weather scrubs Florida launch of Delta rocket.
newsitem.headline: Weather scrubs Florida launch of Delta rocket.

text.p: The launch of a Delta II rocket from the Cape Canaveral Air Force Station was delayed by weather on Sunday.

The launch was to have been the first of a Delta rocket at the cape since a Delta II exploded shortly after takeoff in January, raining debris over the launch complex and sending a cloud of noxious gas spreading along Florida's east coast.
Thick clouds over the launch complex and high upper level winds led mission control to scrub the launch about 7:20 p.m. (2320 GMT).
McDonnell-Douglas officials said they would try to launch the rocket again on Monday at about 6:45 p.m. (2245 GMT).
The $150 million mission was supposed to deliver a Norwegian Thor II communication satellite into Earth orbit.
The satellite, owned by Telenor International, is designed to add up to 75 channels to Scandinavian televisions, company officials said.
The Jan. 17 Delta explosion, the first in more than 300 missions, caused $22 million in damage to the launch complex but no one was seriously injured.

An investigation traced the explosion to a cracked casing in one of Delta's solid rocket boosters, though the cause of that crack was never determined, said Ann Toulouse, director of communication for McDonnell-Douglas.
On May 5 a Delta successfully launched from Vandenberg Air Force Base in California.
